p5_b0.ocr: In the ongoing pursuit of understanding the differential impact of biomarkers in neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD), the data presented in Table 1 provides a comprehensive overview of various modeling approaches employed to assess the significance of specific predictors among patient cohorts.

p5_b4.ocr: Notably, the patient groups are categorized based on the presence of aquaporin-4 (AQP4) antibodies, with AQP4(−) patients comprising 16 individuals and AQP4(+) patients encompassing 53 individuals. The findings underscore the distinct biochemical profiles that may contribute to differing clinical manifestations and disease progression in these subgroups. Moreover, the column detailing P values serves to highlight the statistical significance of the relationships observed, offering crucial insights into the predictive validity of the models employed.

p5_b5.ocr: This analysis not only enhances our understanding of NMOSD pathophysiology but also underscores the importance of tailored therapeutic strategies that consider the underlying immunological differences between AQP4(−) and AQP4(+) patients. Such insights are imperative for advancing personalized medicine approaches in the management of this complex neurological disorder.
